content:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 -> router-traffic-stall: router heartbeats for dedicated pool 'dedicated-usw-2' missing; router fallback policy triggered to region-us-east-1, observed high 5xxs and stalled responses. Paging sam (oncall)

sam: I'm oncall, looking. seeing alerts for: router.fallback.delta, pool.heartbeat.missed, autoscaler.scale-down.churn. Any recent routing or scaling changes? :eyes:

maria: I rolled a routing policy tweak ~09:12 that changes how we treat heartbeat gaps (now prefers fallback after 2 missed heartbeats instead of 3). deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T09:12Z applied to router-service/routing-policy v2.1.4

devon: grabbing metrics. Cloudwatch/metrics: heartbeat_count for dedicated-usw-2 dropped to 0 around 09:15, autoscaler interpreted as zero capacity and marked pool unhealthy, router started routing away. But traffic remained sticky for some customers -> fallback region overloaded and started failing back to us-west in a loop.

sam: ok that explains oscillation. Is this a real capacity drop or a telemetry miss?

maria: looks like telemetry ingestion lag across the capacity-proxy->telemetry pipeline (kinesis backlog spike at 09:14). The router uses that heartbeat metric as primary health signal.

devon: here's a quick view of the anomaly: ```
> metric: pool.heartbeat_count{pool=dedicated-usw-2}
09:10 -> 120
09:13 -> 3
09:14 -> 0
09:15 -> 0
```

sam: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily change router fallback threshold back to 3 missed heartbeats (so we don't immediately route away) 2) pin active variant in routing policy for impacted customers 3) scale dedicated-usw-2 manually if needed. Who can push the policy rollback?

maria: I can rollback the routing-policy to v2.1.3 (pre-change) and set threshold to 3. Rolling now.

maria: rollback complete, router-policy v2.1.3 active. I also disabled region automatic fallback for the short window (set fallback.mode = disabled) so we don't start oscillating.

sam: thanks. devon, can you confirm traffic now?

devon: after rollback we see router traffic staying in us-west and 5xxs dropping from 62% -> 8% in 3 minutes. Latency also stabilizing. Autoscaler still thinks pool is low because telemetry backlog unresolved.

sam: let's manually scale pool to ensure capacity while telemetry recovers. devon, can you run the scale up?

devon: running manual scale: ```
$ rdctl pools scale dedicated-usw-2 --replicas 8 --reason "manual-mitigation-2141592600"
Scaling started -> desired 8
```

deploy-bot: pool scaling job queued (job id: job-2141592625).

emily: (cs) we have two customers on dedicated-usw-2 reporting elevated errors and slow responses for ~25 minutes. I've messaged them with a troubleshooting note and ETA 30m.

sam: good. keep CS updated. Also create a temporary routing-rule to pin their traffic to the current healthy variant (redwood-7b-q4). Maria, can you help?

maria: added per-customer pin for tenant ids [acct-773, acct-191] to use redwood-7b-q4 in us-west. Rule applied.

devon: telemetry backlog (kinesis) processing rate is catching up. heartbeat_count for pool rose to 58 at 09:27 and now reporting normally. Autoscaler will reconcile soon.

sam: nice. any indication why kinesis backlog spiked?

devon: preliminary: a sidecar (capacity-proxy v1.14.2) started logging repeated transient failures to the telemetry API due to a cert rotation that briefly rejected connections at 09:13. That caused a transient drop in emitted heartbeats. The routing policy change made us sensitive to brief drops -> caused immediate fallback decision.

maria: root cause components: 1) cert rotation caused telemetry gap 2) routing policy threshold was too aggressive (2 misses) 3) autoscaler trusts heartbeat exclusively for health decisions (no secondary check).

sam: immediate action items assigned: 
- devon: open CR to add secondary health signal (pool.agent_ping + kernel_metrics) to router health decision (P0 mitigation)
- maria: add a small debounce window to routing policy and revert default to 3 missed heartbeats (done as temporary, follow-up to bake in config flag)
- infra: fix cert rotation to be zero-disruption (on call infra owners)
- cs/emily: follow up with impacted customers and share postmortem ETA

devon: I've kicked off a quick alert to infra team about cert rotation and assigned ticket INF-2141.

maria: also adding an automated rollback guard in deploy pipeline so routing-policy cannot be changed to <3 misses without a safety flag.

sam: status update: rollback + manual scaling + per-tenant pinning applied. Customer errors dropping, telemetry normalizing. Closing pager soon but keep thread open for postmortem notes.

emily: thx team, CS will send interim note to customers in 15 minutes.

sam: final: creating incident ticket INC-214159 for postmortem. Assigning owners: devon (root cause), maria (policy changes), infra (cert rotation). We should have a 72h postmortem.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-214159 created and assigned.

sam: thanks everyone. I'll mark as acknowledged but leave ops follow-up to owners. :thumbsup:
